# Synthetic fingerprint compatibility corpus

These fourteen audio fixtures contain generated chirps, chords and amplitude envelopes, with no third-party recordings. `carrier-results.json` binds lossless carriers, decoded input hashes, the original generator and the separately captured Chromaprint 1.6.2 reference executable/library identities. `reference-results.json` retains the original capture record. Homebrew media tools generated/reference-tested these fixtures only; they are not linked or shipped as application dependencies.

Tests decompress carriers with an independent gzip implementation, verify their original hashes, then run OpenTag's actual embedded Rust API. The same expected fingerprints exercise Apple's vDSP and the bundled KissFFT backend on other CI targets. Normal tests require no `fpcalc` or `ffmpeg` program. The retained Python generators document regeneration and require developer media tools; regenerating fixtures does not establish compatibility without a fresh independent reference capture.

The project-authored synthetic audio inputs and generator code are distributed under OpenTag's MIT license.

## Exact prefix boundary

`exact-prefix-corrupt-tail.flac` is a separate generated regression, outside
the fourteen frozen compatibility cases. It contains 121 one-second FLAC
frames at 11,025 Hz, mono, 16-bit silence. Only the last frame is damaged;
the first 120 frames are unchanged. The test requires the complete prefix to
succeed without decoding that following frame, while retaining the 121-second
stream duration and leaving the input unchanged.

Generate the valid control with a developer-only FFmpeg tool:

```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i anullsrc=r=11025:cl=mono -t 121 -c:a flac -sample_fmt s16 -frame_size 11025 constant121.flac
ffprobe -v error -show_frames -show_entries frame=nb_samples,pkt_pos,pkt_size -of json constant121.flac
```

The retained fixture was generated by FFmpeg 9.0.2. Its 121st packet starts
at byte 10,086, has a ten-byte frame header and is 15 bytes long. Changing
its constant-subframe byte at offset 10,096 from `00` to `7e` requests an
order-32 LPC subframe without its required residual payload. An independent
FFmpeg decoder rejects that frame. The fixture SHA-256 is
`893b27c6a8987e938df63cdd4435324511c444e623e522183d4ea0c446a2e547`.
Normal regression execution uses the embedded producer and bundled bytes;
it invokes neither FFmpeg nor fpcalc.

## DSDIFF input coverage

`dsdiff12.dff.gz` contains twelve seconds of project-authored stereo DSD64,
with a DSDIFF 1.5 `FRM8` form, `PROP/SND` metadata and uncompressed `DSD `
payload. `generate-dsdiff.py` reproduces the carrier using only Python's
standard library. The raw bytes repeat `69` per channel; no recording is used.
`dsdiff-reference.json` records the raw/carrier hashes and the separately
hashed Chromaprint 1.6.2 reference executable's duration/fingerprint result.

The regression first verifies that OpenTag's tag reader accepts the `.dff`
file, then compares the actual embedded producer with that frozen reference
and checks that the input remains unchanged. It passed on the original
reviewed profile before any production change. FFmpeg 9.0.2 handles DSDIFF
through the already enabled `iff` demuxer (`libavformat/iff.c`: `iff_probe`
recognizes `FRM8`/`DSD ` and `ff_iff_demuxer` owns the reader). That pinned
version has no separate `dsdiff` demuxer. This is an additional coverage test;
the fourteen original compatibility cases are unchanged. Normal execution
uses bundled bytes and invokes no external media program.
